messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have set up a line of code to use a "batch" approach to run repetitive runs using a large number of data sets.
The results are easily then written as a CSV table.

BatDistance<- Deducer::descriptive.table (vars = d (BatDistance),data= BatDistance,func.names =c("Valid N","Minimum","Maximum","Median","Mean","St. Deviation","25th Percentile","75th Percentile"),func.additional= list(p10=function(x) quantile(x, c(0.10), na.rm=TRUE),p90=function(x) quantile(x, c(0.90), na.rm=TRUE)))

## Then write the results Change output name and directory for stats.
write.csv(BatDistance,file="C:\\CLN_Bat Project\\Bufered_mine data 2016\\Distance_Stats.csv")

Where/how can I add a "Stratify by" line to the above?

The data frame will always be assigned to BatDistance using BatDistance<-data table
The DF / table read in has 2 columns Bat,distance

I need to stratify the results by Bat so that the CSV table will have rows with the "Stratified by" Bat and columns will have the descriptive stats.

Must be simple to add that?

Cheers,

Bruce

messages.body_plain:
It seems that the behaviour of Deducer's PlotBuilder differs from that given in the docs.

Here it is said that I will be able to select bin size on drawing the histogram plot:

http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.PlotBuilder

However, I'm trying to do this and get only one input field (Variable) in the interface, see the screenshot: http://i.imgur.com/H1FF5Fa.png

Is it a bug or so?

I'm using Mac OS X, R version 3.2, the latest version of Deducer (0.7-7).

--
Sincerely yours,
Ilya V. Schurov.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Ian!

That "histogram" from "Geometric Elements" works fine.

However, according to the screenshots in the docs:

http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.PlotBuilder

there also used "Histogram" from "Templates", but from "Geometric Elements", and the interface is simpler than for those in "Geometric Elements" (e.g. no "Size", "Fill" and so on input fields).

Actually, I'm okay with current solution, but probably the docs are outdated (or something wrong with my installation of Deducer?).

Also, it seem to be strange that template Histogram uses geom_bar instead of geom_histogram (producing completely useless histogram for e.g. rnorm()-generated data).

> data(mtcars)
> corr.mat1<-cor.matrix(variables=d(mpg,carb,carb+rnorm(length(carb))),,
+ data=mtcars,
+ test=cor.test,
+ method='spearman',
+ alternative="two.sided",exact=FALSE)
>
> p<-ggcorplot(corr.mat1,data = mtcars)
Error: Attempted to create layer with no stat.

Are there any ways to solve it?

--
Sincerely yours,
Ilya V. Schurov.
